title_en: Active Learning of Robust Models
abstract_en: In many domains from species identification to cancer diagnosis, labelling data to train predictive models remains costly. In these settings, it is advantageous to intelligently select data points to label to achieve the maximum information gain, this is the motivation behind the study of active learning. In addition to the high costs of acquiring data in such domains, there is the added complexity of data distribution shifts that can occur between training and deployment. For example, the features of cancerous skin cells taken in one country may be different in another region of the world. These two challenges - efficient labelling of data, and learning models robust to distribution shifts have been studied separately but not together, even though these challenges often co-occur in real-life settings. We identify failure modes of standard active learning approaches when the distribution of data at deployment is different from the distribution in which the data is sampled for labelling. We propose a new strategy for efficiently learning classifiers that generalise under specific forms of distribution shift, namely subpopulation shift. Drawing on work in learning from heterogeneous data, we aim to train models that perform well across subpopulations of the data, through active learning. To handle this challenging setting, we exploit the fact that many datasets include metadata about data collection that can serve as a noisy proxy for each sample's underlying subpopulation. We demonstrate how to leverage these noisy labels during active learning selection, and demonstrate empirically that our approach improves classifier accuracy across subpopulations.

title_en: Sparse Array-Inspired Frame Structure Design for 5G NR ISAC
abstract_en: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has emerged as a promising paradigm for future wireless networks. However, the extensive occupation of time-frequency resources for sensing limits the communication capacity. To address the resource conflict, this paper proposes a novel sparse sensing frame structure aligned with the 5G new radio (5G NR) resource grid at the slot and physical resource block (PRB) levels through a predefined sensing-pattern block. Specifically, inspired by the design of two-dimensional (2D) sparse antenna arrays, we map the sparse spatial geometries onto the time-frequency resource grid. By leveraging the hole-free property of the difference coarray, we eliminate the range-velocity ambiguity and cast the sensing signals into a reconstructed higher-order tensor representation. For efficient parameter estimation, we propose a novel binary-tree-based tensor train decomposition (BT-TTD) algorithm that extracts lower-dimensional tensor train cores (TT-cores) and executes a Vandermonde-prior-guided rectified alternating least squares (RecALS) algorithm. Simulation results validate that the proposed scheme achieves competitive estimation accuracy with reduced complexity. Furthermore, we investigate the topological properties of various sparse patterns, revealing the inherent trade-off among sensing accuracy, resource occupancy, and computational complexity.

title_en: A Hybrid Digital/Analog Polyphase Filtering Approach for High-Speed RF-DACs
abstract_en: This paper proposes a hybrid polyphase interpolation for RF-DACs that removes the need for full-rate digital commutation by using passive combining on the RF-DAC itself. A P-branch polyphase FIR filter is factored into M streams, each formed by a (P/M)-way digital commutator at fRF/M and driving a dedicated RF-DAC slice, giving either partial digital (1<M<P) or fully analog (M=P) recombination. We show that the slice array acts as a single full-rate DAC with an M-times longer zero-order hold, derive yield laws for slice gain, timing and unit-capacitor mismatch, and find that with retiming the binding requirement is sub-picosecond matching of the fRF clock arrival, so the best choice is the smallest M that closes digital timing. Two 28-nm digital macros, designed for a 12.8GSps output rate and verified by post-layout simulation, illustrate a 4-phase variant that closes timing up to 14.4GSps with its digital logic at fRF/4 and an 8-phase variant that closes timing up to 16GSps with its digital logic at fRF/8. The analog recombination is evaluated with a behavioral model of the slice array. The architectures target wideband software defined radio (SDR) platforms, including cognitive radio, electronic warfare, and satellite communications.

title_en: PhyCAD: Physics-Aware Text-to-CAD Generation via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
abstract_en: Language-driven computer-aided design (CAD) generation enables the creation of editable parametric models from text, yet geometric correctness alone does not ensure physical feasibility. We present PhyCAD, a framework for physics-aware Text-to-CAD generation that trains language models to produce executable CadQuery programs under geometric and physical constraints. To support this setting, we construct a Text-to-CAD dataset that links parametric CAD models with geometric specifications, loading conditions, and physical constraints. We further develop an automated CAD--CAE verifier that combines program execution, geometric checks, and finite element analysis to provide feedback for model training. A key learning challenge is to prioritize joint satisfaction of geometric and physical constraints while retaining informative feedback on partial progress. A flat aggregation of heterogeneous rewards can obscure this priority, allowing improvements in individual criteria to compensate for unmet design requirements. We therefore introduce a Hierarchical Balanced Advantage for Group Relative Policy Optimization, grouping candidates into levels according to their verification status and combining between-level progress with objective-wise peer ranking within each level. This formulation preserves cross-level priority in the training signal while providing fine-grained feedback for satisfying constraints and improving feasible designs. Experiments across multiple language models show that PhyCAD consistently improves joint geometric and physical constraint satisfaction. These results demonstrate the value of verifiable engineering feedback for advancing language-driven CAD generation beyond geometric reconstruction toward physics-aware design.

title_en: Against All Likelihood
abstract_en: Maximum likelihood is the dominant training principle for large language models, yet likelihood is neither necessary nor sufficient for truth. Unlikely events happen every day, and frequently repeated statements can be false. Drawing on a philosophical tradition that ties objectivity to invariance rather than probability (from Nozick's account of objective facts and Wigner's principles of invariance to the structural realism of Poincaré and Cassirer), we argue that the truth of a statement should be judged not by its probability under a single distribution, but by its invariance across relevant transformations of the environment. We connect this view to machine learning literature on out-of-distribution generalization and invariant learning, sketch how invariance could be tested at inference time with language models, and discuss implications for continual learning.

title_en: KineCouple: Substrate-conditioned residual readout for enzyme kinetic prediction
abstract_en: Accurate prediction of enzyme kinetic parameters can support enzyme engineering and metabolic modeling by complementing experimental characterization. Existing prediction methods often pool residue-level protein features before combining them with substrate features. Such substrate-independent pooling cannot adapt residue weighting to the substrate during aggregation, potentially diluting information relevant to a specific enzyme-substrate pair. Since the contributions of individual residues to catalysis can depend on the substrate, substrate-conditioned aggregation offers a way to emphasize residue features relevant to the prediction. We introduce KineCouple, which uses substrate queries and residue-level keys and values in cross-attention, allowing the substrate to guide residue selection before aggregation. The model preserves the global protein representation and adds a gated correction defined as the difference between the conditioned readout and a uniform readout. ProtT5 and MolT5 remain frozen, and separate models predict kcat and Km on a logarithmic scale. In pooled out-of-fold predictions on the CataPro benchmarks, KineCouple reduces kcat RMSE from 1.333 to 1.330 and increases PCC from 0.492 to 0.496 relative to reproduced CataPro. For Km, RMSE decreases from 0.998 to 0.997 and PCC increases from 0.633 to 0.634. Spearman correlation also improves for both tasks.

title_en: Scalable BLE Channel Sounding Localization with Ranging-Assisted PDoA
abstract_en: Bluetooth Channel Sounding (CS) enables accurate phase-based ranging, but multi-anchor localization requires sequential ranging exchanges that limit scalability and increase measurement latency. This paper proposes Ranging-Assisted Phase Difference of Arrival (RA-PDoA), a scalable BLE localization architecture combining one active anchor performing a standard two-way CS exchange with multiple passive receive-only anchors observing the same transmissions. A channel-recovery framework is derived that enables passive anchors to reconstruct a channel response suitable for super-resolution delay estimation, allowing multipath-robust ranging without participating in a two-way exchange. Coarse arrival-time information is further used to bound the position estimate and reject inconsistent range solutions. A comprehensive evaluation characterizes the impact of multipath propagation, body shadowing, synchronization requirements, oscillator impairments, anchor placement, and deployment inaccuracies, thereby quantifying the practical infrastructure requirements for scalable BLE localization. Simulation results in modeled indoor environments show that RA-PDoA reduces the 90th-percentile localization error from 175.3 cm to 95.5 cm under body shadowing while maintaining an airtime requirement independent of the number of anchors. The results demonstrate that a single active ranging link enables scalable and multipath-robust BLE Channel Sounding localization.

title_en: Pinching Antenna Systems (PASS) for Air-Ground Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC)
abstract_en: This paper proposes a multi-user single-target air-ground integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, in which a ground pinching-antenna system (PASS) transmits communication and sensing signals and an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) receives the target echo. The communication and sensing beamforming vectors, pinching antenna positions, and UAV position are jointly optimized to minimize the weighted Cramér-Rao bound (CRB). A penalty dual decomposition (PDD) algorithm is developed for the resulting nonconvex problem. The auxiliary variable and beamforming subproblems admit globally optimal solutions in semi-closed form, while the positions of the pinching antennas and the UAV are updated by successive convex approximation (SCA). Under mild conditions, every accumulation point of the sequence generated by our proposed algorithm is a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) point of the reformulated problem. Numerical results show that the proposed PASS-UAV design achieves a lower weighted CRB than conventional multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) and PASS benchmarks.

title_en: Beyond the Pseudo-Inverse: GIM Precoding for Per-Antenna Power Minimisation in MU-MIMO
abstract_en: We study linear precoder design for multi-user MIMO downlink under per-antenna power constraints (PAPC), which arise naturally when each antenna port has its own power amplifier. While the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse is the unique optimal generalized inverse for zero-forcing precoding under a total power constraint [1], we prove this optimality does not extend to the MMSE/RZF case under PAPC. Any precoder in the Generalized Inverse Matrix (GIM) family shares the same effective channel and per-user SINRs as the pseudo-inverse baseline, while its null-space component reshapes the per-antenna power profile. This separation principle enables minimising peak per-antenna power at fixed SINR targets with zero SINR penalty. We characterise the convex peak-power problem over this family and its active-set optimality, establish MRT and ZF asymptotic limits, and provide a convergent first-order subgradient algorithm. Simulations with 8-64 antennas confirm gains of 1.9-3.7 dB over pseudo-inverse RZF, with GIM-MMSE eliminating essentially all PAPC violations up to 20% per-antenna budget imbalance. The framework applies directly to fully-digital massive MIMO. Cell-free and hybrid analog-digital arrays are promising extensions.

title_en: DNN-Driven Proactive UAV Trajectory and Beam Steering for Blockage-Resilient Communications
abstract_en: This paper proposes Autonomous UAV Communication (AutUAVCom), a proactive communication system that jointly adapts the flight trajectory and RF beam steering to minimize UAV energy consumption while satisfying secrecy and reliability requirements for rescue teams operating in dynamic, cluttered, and GPS-denied environments. Unlike existing modelbased proactive approaches, AutUAVCom employs a deep neural network-based Tracking and Prediction (T&P) module that combines onboard sensing with spatiotemporal and body-orientation information to track users, localize blocking objects, and predict future trajectories and potential beam blockages. Building on the T&P module, we formulate a constrained optimization problem and develop a two-step iterative numerical approach. Monte Carlo simulations show that, relative to a reactive system, AutUAVCom achieves 10% and 19% gains in energy efficiency and channel secrecy, respectively, while reducing the outage probability by 85%, under a mean blockage arrival interval of 120 seconds and a mean blockage duration of 20 seconds.

title_en: Robust Deep Prototype Classifiers via Lipschitz Training
abstract_en: Robustness and interpretability are interrelated and desirable properties of machine learning models. A model that changes its prediction under imperceptible perturbations behaves inconsistently with human-recognizable features and, hence, is not interpretable. Prototype-based classifiers such as Generalized Learning Vector Quantization address both at once. They are interpretable by construction because they make the decision by comparing the input to the prototypical example; and their hypothesis margin yields a closed form robustness certificate. However, on high-dimensional data, these shallow models need deep embedding networks to achieve high accuracy, and this voids the robustness certificate. The margin is a statement about distances in the embedding space, and an unconstrained network can map an arbitrarily small input perturbation to arbitrarily large attacks in the embedding space. We close this gap with a theorem: if the embedding network is locally L-Lipschitz around a point, and the classifier is ε-robust around its embedding, then the full model is ε/L-robust in the input space. Based on this, we propose a Lipschitz training scheme to achieve L-Lipschitz properties for embedding networks. We evaluate three classification heads (linear, linear Support Vector Machine, and GLVQ) crossed with two embedding networks (standard and Lipschitz-constrained) on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Imagenette-160, under FGS, PGD and C\&W attacks. The evaluation results show that combining a prototype-based head with a Lipschitz-constrained embedding provides the strongest robustness. This suggests that the Lipschitz constraint provides an additional robustness benefit in addition to the advantage provided by the prototype-based head. Since the Lipschitz constraint is enforced by sampling rather than by construction, the reported robustness is empirical rather than certified.

title_en: Model-based learning for DoA estimation and array calibration via continuous sparse recovery
abstract_en: Direction of arrival (DoA) estimation, a classical signal processing problem, has experienced renewed interest with the advent of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). While decades of research have yielded highly accurate DoA estimators, hardware impairments have frequently been neglected, despite degrading both DoA estimation accuracy and downstream communication performance in ISAC systems. This work introduces a joint array calibration and DoA estimation method based on the simultaneous orthogonal matching pursuit (SOMP) algorithm, following the model-based machine learning paradigm. The proposed method enables the calibration of antenna arrays subject to severe gain-phase and antenna location impairments through projected gradient descent (PGD), with either supervised or unsupervised objectives. Additionally, DoA estimation is enhanced by extending SOMP to continuous dictionaries via PGD refinement steps. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method enables efficient hardware impairment compensation, even without labeled samples, while outperforming conventional sparse recovery and subspace-based DoA estimation baselines.

title_en: Fused-Softmax for efficient quantized attention
abstract_en: Low-precision matrix throughput on modern GPUs is growing far faster than vector-arithmetic throughput. Attention therefore cannot realize the available GEMM performance because softmax has become the pipeline bottleneck. We introduce Fused-Softmax Attention, a training-free algorithm that reformulates and approximates softmax to fold its dominant operations into the attention GEMMs, moving work from vector units to matrix cores. Implemented for the AMD CDNA 4 architecture, our MXFP8, MXFP6 and MXFP4 kernels reach approximately 3.0, 4.0 and 4.6 PFLOP/s on an AMD Instinct MI355X GPU, yielding speedups of $2.1\times$, $2.8\times$ and $3.2\times$ over the BF16 attention. Importantly, the additional error introduced by Fused-Softmax remains below the error floor set by quantizing the GEMM operands. On Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, a hybrid MXFP6/4 schedule delivers up to $2.05\times$ end-to-end speedup while preserving the visual quality of the outputs. The kernels ship in AMD's open-source AITER library, and they powered AMD's MLPerf Inference v6.1 Wan2.2 submission, which ran $1.7\times$ faster than AMD's previous-round result on the same hardware. Our results show that redesigning softmax to utilize the matrix pipeline enables attention to capitalize on continued growth in low-precision matrix throughput.

title_en: Safe Reinforcement Learning via Probabilistic Option Shielding
abstract_en: Shielding is a safe reinforcement learning technique that provides safety guarantees while learning, by blocking unsafe actions. Traditional shielding relies on a complete model of the environment to provide long-term guarantees. Probabilistic logic shielding (PLS) lifts the requirement of having such model, but only considers safety in the short term, typically looking only one or few steps ahead. We propose Probabilistic Option Shielding (POS), which extends PLS to the option level, recovering long-horizon safety without reintroducing the need for a complete environment model. POS learns a model-free critic directly from one-step PLS signals, to estimate the probability that an entire option will complete safely under uncertainty. We evaluate POS on safe navigation tasks in the LogiCity environment, and show that it achieves considerably safer training while matching the task performance of standard step-level PLS and other safety related reinforcement learning baselines.

title_en: Circuit Theory-Informed AI for Condition Monitoring in Power Electronics
abstract_en: Artificial intelligence for power electronics is evolving toward a deeper comprehension of system intrinsic behaviors and dynamics. As a novel integration of neural computation and electric circuits, spike-based neuromorphic computing offers promising potential in high energy efficiency and adaptability for data-driven applications. Building on the latency-coding principles, this article proposes a framework for data-light condition monitoring that relies solely on three-phase AC current measurements. The AC current signals are encoded as membrane potentials of RC-based spiking neurons, which are inherently compatible with spiking neural networks that can effectively facilitate the estimation of device parameters. Case studies are presented to validate the performances, while constraints and further optimizations are also evaluated and discussed, and future extensions of the methodology are provided.

title_en: TouchAnnotator: Multi-Source Tactile Supervision with Privileged-View Distillation
abstract_en: Egocentric video captures human-object interaction at scale but rarely includes tactile labels for hidden contact and pressure. We introduce TouchAnnotator, an ego-only bimanual tactile annotator trained with multi-source tactile supervision and privileged-view distillation. A canonical hand field unifies glove pressure, geometry-derived human contact, and robot fingertip deformation from six datasets and three embodiments, while source-aware masks preserve valid targets. During training, an EMA teacher observes synchronized ego and wrist views and distills hand-local representations and tactile predictions into a student that uses only ego video and estimated pose at inference. Compact past-clip memory supplies temporal context. We evaluate on EgoTouch, zero-shot FPHA transfer, and 860 synchronized glove recordings. The model transfers to bare-hand contact and produces qualitatively coherent tactile responses across bare-hand, gloved-hand, and robot embodiments. On measured recordings, it improves temporal accuracy by 5.38 points and Volumetric IoU by 5.02 points under a shared protocol. These results show that heterogeneous human--robot supervision and privileged training views can turn egocentric video into dense tactile annotations.

title_en: DeepRT-Cal: Learning to Calibrate Ray-Traced Twin Channel Statistics with Low-Fidelity Environmental Geometry
abstract_en: Sixth-generation (6G) wireless systems increasingly rely on digital twin channels (DTCs) to represent and interact with physical radio environments. Ray tracing (RT) is naturally suited to DTC construction because it provides deterministic and physically interpretable channel predictions. However, high-fidelity three-dimensional environment models are expensive to obtain, whereas geometric inaccuracies in low-fidelity models can alter the detected multipath components (MPCs) and consequently distort received-power and delay-domain twin channel statistics. Building on the DeepRT ray-tracing framework, this paper proposes DeepRT-Cal, a geometry-aware cross-fidelity calibration framework that predicts high-fidelity twin channel statistics from low-fidelity geometry and RT features.The network encodes global link descriptors, masked low-fidelity MPC tokens, propagation-corridor geometry, and link-centered environmental objects. During training, detailed geometry is introduced as privileged information with structured masking, while deployment requires only low-fidelity geometry and low-fidelity RT information. A link-conditioned cross-attention module retrieves the environmental context relevant to each Tx--Rx link. The prediction heads estimate high-fidelity twin channel statistics, including total received power, RMS delay spread, mean excess delay, and a normalized power-weighted power-delay profile (PDP). Outdoor evaluation shows that, in an non-line of sight (NLoS) region, the method reduces power MAE from 16.80 to 3.88 dB and RMS delay-spread MAE from 304.89 to 98.19 ns. In a LoS-dominated region, power prediction improves, while RMS delay-spread accuracy remains comparable to direct RT.

title_en: Equidistribution of Solution Gradients in Physics-Informed Neural Networks via Coordinate Transformations
abstract_en: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) often struggle to approximate solutions with sharp gradients due to optimization difficulties and spectral bias. Motivated by the principle of gradient equidistribution from the stretching approach in grid generation, which redistributes solution gradients to reduce functional complexity, we propose Coordinate Transformation PINNs (CTPINNs), which incorporate learnable coordinate transformations to map the physical domain into a computational domain where the physical solutions become approximately affine, making them easier for neural networks to learn. We propose two constructions of the transformation: an explicit construction based on Majorants and an implicit construction based on invertable neural networks. Experimentally, the explicit construction can improve accuracy for PDEs with available explicit coordinate transformations, and the implicit construction can be combined with other advanced PINN models as an efficient plug-in module to improve performance across a range of challenging PDE benchmarks.

title_en: Optimal Probabilistic Answer Set Programming: Complexity and Implementations
abstract_en: Probabilistic Answer Set Programming (PASP) extends Answer Set Programming with the possibility of representing uncertain data. Among the possible available semantics, we focus here on the credal semantics. In this setting, prior work has focused exclusively on plain ASP programs, i.e., programs without optimization constructs. However, many real world tasks define optimality criteria over the possible solutions, which cannot be conveniently modeled with existing probabilistic ASP frameworks. In this paper, we close this gap and propose optimal Probabilistic Answer Set Programming, which extends PASP by also allowing weak constraints, which are the standard optimization construct of ASP. We define the semantics of such programs, study the computational complexity of the inference and most probable explanation tasks, and propose practical implementations based on Algebraic Model Counting and Answer Set Programming with Quantifiers. An empirical evaluation of the proposed approach on three real world tasks confirms the applicability of our framework.

title_en: Capital Efficiency, Isolation, Risk, and Ruin in Generative AI Inference Serving Infrastructure
abstract_en: Generative AI serving is an extremely capital-intensive endeavor that demands rapid, step-change improvements in capital efficiency to prevent industry wide increases in the cost of capital from limiting growth plans. Keeping pace with the economic necessities will increasingly require infrastructure providers to confront operationally-inconvenient realities of production serving, including the extreme heterogeneity of generative AI request costs. We have explored workload isolation as a foundational, fleet-level lever for increasing capital efficiency. Isolation is the practice of intelligently grouping "like" requests before execution. Rather than exposing every replica to the full heterogeneous workload distribution, isolation deliberately reshapes the workload presented to the hardware by assigning requests with different cost characteristics to different portions of the fleet. Workload isolation on its own does not make expensive requests cheaper; it prevents a costly portion of the workload from unnecessarily determining the operating point and capital efficiency of the entire fleet. It additionally lays the foundational groundwork that can serve as a launching point for compounding gains via narrow-band optimizations (tailoring) and custom silicon designs while also informing up on pricing policy. This paper uses representative production data and experience to convey the motivation behind isolation as a fleet-level lever for increased capital efficiency.

title_en: Capacity of Multi-Layer Manhattan-Grid UAV Corridors Served by Terrestrial 5G NR Networks
abstract_en: Advanced air mobility (AAM) is expected to organize unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) traffic into corridors at multiple altitudes. In this paper, we study the downlink (DL) and uplink (UL) capacity of a multi-layer Manhattan-grid corridor mesh served by a terrestrial fifth-generation (5G) new radio (NR) macro network. The corridor spacing and the numbers of layers, UAVs, and base stations are configurable. We combine the 3GPP aerial channel and antenna models, correlated UAV mobility, and frequency-selective fading with an NR physical-layer abstraction that includes channel aging and link adaptation. Results show that UAVs above 90 m experience a DL signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) about 17 dB below that of ground users, and that a dense macro network with $10^\circ$ downtilt leaves 17-29% of corridor positions without DL service under full-buffer load, regardless of corridor spacing. On a common layout, the carrier frequency (700 MHz, 3.5 GHz, or 7.2 GHz) changes the UAV SINR by less than 0.5 dB, since the corridor links are strongly interference-limited. The UL is the bottleneck: at 85% satisfaction, a 20 MHz carrier supports only about 3.4-4.1 UAVs/km$^2$ with 4 Mb/s of UL video per UAV.

title_en: Rethinking Optimization Methods for Hierarchical Feature Selection
abstract_en: Rare-event forecasting often depends on interpretable conjunctions: a single keyword, location, or temporal cue may be weak, while their joint occurrence can identify a meaningful precursor. Hierarchical-Task Numerical conjunctive feature Learning (HTNL) selects Numerical Conjunctive Features (NCFs) through a structured sparsity objective. However, the resulting optimization problem is challenging, making optimization design critical to its practical performance. We give a unified diagnosis of four HTNL optimization families: original majorization-minimization (MM), variational quadratic form (VQF), alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), and weighted group lasso (WGL). Our analysis distinguishes three key factors that jointly determine HTNL optimization behavior. First, VQF and MM are algebraically equivalent under matched variational updates and optimize a squared-penalty formulation. Second, ADMM optimizes the unsquared objective through consensus splitting; we replace its truncated FISTA proximal solver with a scalar bisection update (ADMM-Bisect) for more accurate treatment of near-threshold blocks. Third, WGL targets the same unsquared objective, while all methods face rapidly decaying active-set admission scores. Across two synthetic datasets and 11 civil-unrest and flu-surveillance tasks, VQF achieves the highest mean AUC with the most compact non-collapsing supports. ADMM-Bisect reduces measured runtime, while calibrated WGL avoids the empty-support failures of its original scale. Synthetic results further show how proximal accuracy, pruning, and search budget affect candidate recovery, especially for longer conjunctions. Code will be made publicly available upon publication.

title_en: ResQAdam: Residual-Preserving Adaptive Optimization for Memory-Efficient Quantization Aware Training
abstract_en: Quantization-aware training (QAT) is the most reliable way to obtain accurate low-bit large language models (LLMs), but training with AdamW keeps two dense FP32 states for every weight matrix. We find that low-rank memory-efficient optimizers such as GaLore and LDAdam degrade substantially in QAT. A considerable part of the QAT momentum lies outside its top-r singular subspace, and projection-based methods discard this part at every step. We further observe that this residual remains useful when only its sign is kept. Based on these observations, we propose ResQAdam. It keeps a single BF16 momentum, applies Adam only to the r x r coordinates of the principal subspace, and adds a normalized sign update computed from the residual. We evaluate ResQAdam with two from-scratch QAT methods and three QAT fine-tuning pipelines, with weights quantized down to 2 bits. It reduces optimizer-state memory by 71% to 74% relative to AdamW, stays close to AdamW in most settings, and lowers training throughput by less than 2%.

title_en: Who's Asking? Audience-Conditioned Privatization
abstract_en: The abundance of user-generated conversational data makes the question of how to responsibly derive insights from confidential data without putting the individuals in it at risk ever more important. However, the majority of existing differentially private (DP) synthetic text generation (SDG) and anonymization approaches ignore the context of the data's downstream usage, which results in loss of important information. DP-SDG provides the same guarantee regardless of the recipient, and anonymization relies on predefined attribute categories. They both ignore the observation that an attribute that is harmless to one audience can be sensitive to another, and each audience typically needs only some attributes preserved. We propose Ext-Classify-Priv, a framework that (1) extracts the information types present in a corpus, (2) classifies which of them are private for a given audience following contextual integrity, and (3) protects only those attributes, using either anonymization or SDG with Feature-DP approaches. On Reddit data with 3 audiences, our audience-specific releases are more faithful than a single audience-agnostic release for every audience. On bioRxiv data, our SDG method improves MAUVE from 0.097 to 0.420 at epsilon=1 and on the proprietary real estate data, our anonymization method improves MAUVE from 0.698 to 0.959 over the best baselines.

title_en: The Relational Capacity Framework: A Lens for AI-Mediated Relationality
abstract_en: A growing literature examines the impact of engaging with AI chatbots on our relationality: our ability to form relationships with others, maintain them through life's changes, and exit when needed. title_en: Adaptive Scheduling Pipeline for Multi-Instance Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning
abstract_en: We present the Adaptive Scheduling Pipeline (ASP), an offline rollout scheduler for multi-instance asynchronous reinforcement learning (RL) of large language models (LLMs). ASP jointly reduces three sources of rollout underutilization - padding bubbles from intra-minibatch length heterogeneity, skewness bubbles from long-tail outputs, and sorting bubbles from fluctuations in training-queue occupancy induced by length-sorted dispatch - through a single offline preprocessing pass. This enables efficient multi-instance rollout that overcomes the early scaling plateau of single-instance inference while smoothing the arrival of generated samples at the trainer. We integrate the scheduler into an asynchronous architecture that decouples rollout from training while keeping policy lag observable and bounded. Complete ASP improves end-to-end throughput by up to 3.22 times and reduces iteration time by up to 76.8% relative to MindSpeed-RL, while reducing iteration time by up to 62.5% relative to verl. Within ASP, scheduling reduces mean iteration time by 10.9%. ASP also scales more robustly with additional generation resources than these baselines and shows no visible convergence degradation in the measured bounded-lag regime. ASP has since been used in an internal telecom-domain RL post-training workflow, reducing the reported training period from more than three months to about two months and producing a domain-enhanced model for knowledge answering and tool calling.

title_en: Learning Whom to Trust About the Unseen: Source Credibility and Reliability Transfer in Language Models
abstract_en: A source who has been right before deserves attention, but about what? We ask how far a demonstrated record of reliability travels in language models when the new claim cannot be checked, and whether the answer depends on the kind of claim. Three behavioral studies across six models approach the question from three angles. Study 1 adapts the Einstein-effect paradigm and finds that models, unlike the human sample, favor a spiritual leader over a scientist for the same obscure statement, and that the preference largely reverses when the statement is reworded in the vocabulary of physics. Study 2 adapts a paradigm in which a trusted expert calls a scientific or religious explanation unknown or a mystery; models reproduce the human domain asymmetry in exaggerated form. Study 3, the central test, gives two fictional informants different records on checkable river forecasts and then has them endorse matched claims about hidden natural and spiritual causes of the same village events. Most models carry the record to natural causes and barely at all to spiritual ones; one model transfers it weakly to either. Telling the model that the reliable informant forecasts by spiritual guidance rather than by measurement lowers that informant's influence on natural claims in every model and produces no comparable gain on spiritual claims in any. Demonstrated reliability thus has a scope in these models, and the account a source gives of how they came to be reliable can narrow it. Whether this reflects a judgment about relevance or the low prior credence of spiritual claims is the question the design leaves open, and we outline the experiment that would settle it.

title_en: Global Solar Siting from Geospatial Embeddings
abstract_en: Global solar photovoltaic (PV) capacity is rapidly growing, helping decrease our emissions and dependence on fossil fuels. However, optimally siting a solar plant remains challenging, requiring anticipation of geographical, urban, and infrastructure needs. Current methods rely on multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) using hand-picked geophysical layers and solar-resource products, however these strategies are not geographically transferable and do not capture the practical requirements of solar sites. We use geospatial embeddings, dense vectors representing geophysical properties of a location, to analyse 38,591 existing solar sites and the land they were built on to learn the latent solar suitability signal. We assess a set of linear and non-linear models and select a soft-voting ensemble of a random forest and a multilayer perceptron (RF+MLP ensemble), chosen for accuracy and large scale deployability. Validated against future installations in thirteen countries, the ensemble separates existing solar sites from random land with a median ROC-AUC of 0.90. Compared with published MCDA strategies, the ensemble increases ROC-AUC by 0.06-0.30 in every country. The ranking also concentrates real deployment: the most-suitable 20% of land holds 84% of estimated generation (annual energy yield) and 67% of installed capacity (potential power output). After applying standard siting constraints, 5.6% of global land (9.8% if cropland is permitted) remains highly suited to solar. The global 10 m resolution solar suitability dataset and code can be found here: https://github.com/Abdullahr29/Global-Solar-Siting.

title_en: Energy-Aware Vertically Layered Pinching-Antenna System Design with Probabilistic LoS Availability
abstract_en: This paper investigates a vertically layered pinching antenna (PA) system, in which dielectric waveguides deployed at different heights provide additional vertical spatial degrees of freedom for line-of-sight (LoS)-favorable PA placement. title_en: Semantic Conditional Similarity (SCS): A Formal Mathematical Framework
abstract_en: Semantic Textual Similarity (STS) operates on document pairs, returning a single scalar per comparison. In a multi-document setting where several sources may have contributed to one or more targets, pairwise STS cannot disentangle each source's marginal semantic contribution from their shared vocabulary. In this paper, Semantic Conditional Similarity (SCS) is introduced as a conditional form of STS that computes similarity between two documents after eliminating semantic elements shared with a third via set-theoretic operations. SCS makes four contributions: 1) it introduces directionality, partitioning pairwise relations into lateral (inter-source) and vertical (source-to-target) classes; 2) conditioning induces role-dependent asymmetry by extending the comparison domain from unordered pairs to ordered, conditioned triples of a target, a reference, and a conditioning document; 3) SCS introduces inter-document conditioning by subtracting shared content from a third document, complementing the intra-document conditioning in recent C-STS work; and 4) the set-theoretic decomposition achieves threshold-free partitioning of shared and residual content, requiring no arbitrary similarity cutoff. Although developed for the $n \to 1$ configuration, the framework extends to $1 \to n$ via vertical role reversal and to $m \to n$ via independent composition of source- and target-side conditioning. With the established $1 \to 1$ case, these span the full spectrum of document cardinality. SCS scores should be interpreted ordinally, as rankings of marginal contributions rather than absolute measurements. The broader implication is that metric space axioms commonly assumed in similarity formalizations constrain expressiveness in role-differentiated multi-document settings, and that extending the domain to conditioned triples can recover information that pairwise-symmetric comparisons suppress.

title_en: Training Stability under Adaptive Curricula
abstract_en: Unsupervised Environment Design (UED) approaches train reinforcement learning (RL) agents on diverse curricula that may evolve with their capabilities. While prior work has largely focused on how these curricula are constructed, we study whether their students remain trainable under the resulting distributions. Across multiple UED mechanisms, environment complexities, and extended training horizons, we identify recurring learner-side pathologies, including parameter growth, degraded value--outcome ordering, and loss of representational diversity, that accompany stagnation and performance degradation. These findings connect limitations in UED to optimization failures previously identified in conventional deep RL, while showing how adaptive curricula couple the learner's optimization state to its future training distribution. Controlled interventions show that mitigating selected pathologies improves learning. Stabilizing the learner improves long-horizon performance and zero-shot generalization without changing the curriculum rule or increasing environment interaction. Our results establish learner trainability as a complementary design principle for UED. Effective curricula require students that remain capable of learning from the distributions they produce.

title_en: On Lipschitz Explosion in Deep Neural Networks with Normalization: Consequences for Optimization and Adversarial Robustness
abstract_en: Can a network look stable at every layer and still be exponentially unstable as a whole? The Lipschitz constant of a neural network is a basic stability quantity appearing in optimization guarantees, generalization bounds, and robustness certificates. Deep networks naturally admit two such notions, input Lipschitzness, measuring sensitivity to data perturbations, and parameter Lipschitzness, measuring sensitivity to weight perturbations. We prove that, for deep networks with normalization layers, with batch normalization as the canonical example, both Lipschitz constants can grow exponentially with depth and hence with parameter dimension, even under strong per-layer norm control such as $\|W_\ell\|_2\le 1$, and already for linear activations. Thus, a mechanism widely used to stabilize training can create severe worst-case instabilities that are invisible locally, i.e., from layerwise norm bounds alone. Parameter-Lipschitz explosion turns Lipschitz-dependent nonsmooth optimization guarantees into exponential-in-dimension bounds for deep normalized networks, while input-Lipschitz explosion makes worst-case Lipschitz-based generalization and robustness certificates vacuous. The latter also yields a concrete rank-separation mechanism for adversarial vulnerability. The theory predicts that perturbations introducing new singular directions should be amplified much more strongly than perturbations at the same noise level that remain within the input's original singular subspace. Experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 support this prediction, showing that rank-creating perturbations cause substantially sharper drops in accuracy, confidence, and margins than same-subspace perturbations.

title_en: Tags Helping Tags: Coordination-Free Power Boosting for Battery-less Backscatter Networks
abstract_en: Battery-less backscatter sensor nodes powered by radio-frequency wireless power transfer are attractive for large or hard-to-reach deployments, but their range is typically limited by the forward power-transfer link rather than by communication sensitivity. On a hardware testbed, helpers using discrete impedance control are shown to increase the target tag's harvested power by over 50% above an all-absorbing baseline, while randomly set helper impedances give no reliable benefit, and are sometimes even detrimental. We further propose and implement a local algorithm that lets each helper tune its own impedance using only measurements of the target's packet rate, without channel estimation or coordination between helpers, and we show that it brings the target's packet rate close to that of an independently tuned configuration. title_en: Blind Noise Equalization for Large Data Matrices under General Variance Profiles
abstract_en: Low-rank approximation is a basic tool for inference from large and noisy data matrices. However, when noise variances differ across entries, a setting known as heteroskedasticity, the noise can distort the observed spectrum, producing spurious components and obscuring weak signals. To address these challenges, we develop BRINE (Blind Resolvent-based Iterative Noise Equalizer), a data-driven procedure that iteratively rescales rows and columns to equalize the average noise variance across both dimensions. Under suitable conditions, this procedure restores the Marchenko-Pastur law for the noise spectrum and can amplify signal components without prior knowledge of the signal or noise structure. A key idea underlying our approach is to equalize the diagonal entries of the data resolvent as a proxy for equalizing the unknown noise variances. At the population level, we identify a potential function that characterizes this equalization and motivates an iterative minimization procedure. We prove convergence of the iterations to the true equalizer for arbitrary positive variance profiles, with a geometric rate under mild conditions. The updates can be estimated directly from noisy data, and we establish probabilistic error bounds for the scaling factors. Simulations and experiments across diverse biological data modalities and preprocessing pipelines illustrate the effectiveness of our approach.

title_en: Multi-Model Over-the-Air Federated Learning via Transceiver Beamforming and Device Grouping
abstract_en: This paper considers uplink communication design for training multiple independent machine learning models via wireless federated learning. title_en: Remembering Is Not Enough: Evaluating Timing and Omission in Longitudinal AI Mental Health Support
abstract_en: Evaluations of large language models (LLMs) for mental health support commonly focus on the clinical appropriateness of individual responses, potentially overlooking failures that emerge across extended interactions. title_en: Transporting the Past: An Optimal Transport View of Backtracking Counterfactuals
abstract_en: We study backtracking counterfactual inference for Structural Causal Models (SCMs) through the lens of optimal transport. In SCMs, a factual observation generally induces a posterior distribution over exogenous variables, making counterfactual inference inherently distributional. We introduce two complementary frameworks that transport this posterior onto the set of exogenous configurations satisfying a desired counterfactual query. The first constructs a natural pointwise projection and is suitable when the transported exogenous distribution can be used directly. The second enforces mutual independence among counterfactual exogenous variables, so that the transported variables remain interpretable as genuine exogenous noises of the same SCM. We show that both frameworks are consistent with the original backtracking counterfactual principle, and we propose marginal, penalty-based, and hard-constrained solvers for finite-posterior settings. Synthetic experiments on non-bijective SCMs illustrate the geometry of the problem and reveal trade-offs among transport cost, counterfactual constraint satisfaction, and preservation of exogenous independence.

title_en: A Gamma-Mixture Solution for Definite Noncentral Complex Gaussian Quadratic Forms
abstract_en: Finding exact solutions for the statistics of definite noncentral complex Gaussian quadratic forms (CGQFs) has long been a challenging problem. Among existing exact approaches, Raphaeli's formulation [1] remains the most computationally efficient. However, its analytical tractability is hindered by the dependence of its series coefficients on the evaluation variable, which confines their statistics to the probability density function (PDF) and cumulative distribution function (CDF). This paper overcomes this limitation by deriving novel Gamma-mixture representations for the PDF and CDF of positive- and negative-definite noncentral CGQFs. The resulting structure broadens Raphaeli's statistical framework beyond the PDF and CDF to a wider class of CGQF functionals and a substantial range of practical applications. In particular, expectations of integrable functions of definite noncentral CGQFs are expressed as weighted sums of the corresponding expectations over Gamma random variables, enabling the direct derivation of moments, transforms, and performance measures. Moreover, the proposed formulation reduces the single-point complexity from \(O\!\left(n^2K+nK^2\right)\) for Raphaeli's method to \(O\!\left(nK+K^2\right)\), where \(n\) denotes the quadratic-form dimension and \(K\) the truncation order. The proposed Gamma-mixture structure also enables closed-form approximations that, by construction, remain valid probability distributions for any truncation order. In addition, uniform PDF and CDF truncation-error bounds are derived, allowing prescribed-accuracy truncation. As a sample application, we derive the first reported exact average bit error rate expression for maximal-ratio combining receivers with an arbitrary number of branches under an arbitrary positive-definite Rician correlation structure.

title_en: Greedy Byte-Pair Encoding Achieves at Least 0.361 of the Optimal Compression
abstract_en: Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) builds a tokeniser by repeatedly merging a most frequent adjacent pair of symbols; its utility is the total reduction in string length achieved by $k$ merges. It was known that this greedy rule achieves at least a third of the optimal reduction. We prove that it always achieves at least 0.361 of the optimal reduction in string length, for every string, every budget and every tie-breaking rule; this is the first improvement of the bound one third. We also explain why one third was a barrier: the pair-packing relaxation behind it is tight, so a better bound must use more of the optimum's structure. When greedy destroys three of the optimum's merge points at once, one of them can usually be moved next door, because all copies of a rule of the optimum look alike; the remaining cases are paid for later. Along the way we determine the worst-case ratio for two merges exactly, bound it for three, and isolate a single inequality that would settle the problem.

title_en: BEVCast: Path-Adaptive BEV for Efficient End-to-End Autonomous Driving
abstract_en: Camera-based driving models build a dense bird's-eye-view (BEV) grid and spend the same computation on every cell of it, although the vehicle crosses only a few of those cells within the planning horizon. title_en: Physical Sensing Verification for Cognitive ISAC against UAV Spoofing via Digital Twins
abstract_en: As integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) lets 5G and 6G base stations detect drones, software agents will soon act on what they sense. abstract_en: AI-Scientists arrived, but a world for them to grow in did not. title_en: Label-Wording Augmentation in a Typed-Decision Encoder: Gains on Unfamiliar Words, Not on Abbreviations or Codes

title_en: Polarity Classification with Multitask Learning Syntax Augmentation
abstract_en: Sentiment Analysis (SA) is a fundamental NLP task concerned with the identification and categorization of subjective information in text. While lexicon-based methods offer transparency, they often struggle with linguistic phenomena such as negation and intensification. Syntactic parsing has been integrated into SA pipelines to address this, but conventional parsers introduce significant computational overhead. Recent work shows that reformulating dependency parsing as a Sequence Labeling (SEL) task can improve efficiency. We propose and compare two strategies for integrating syntactic knowledge into a neural sentiment analysis model under unified Multi-Task Learning (MTL). The first, Standard-MTL, jointly learns dependency parsing (via sequence labeling) and sentiment polarity classification using a shared encoder with two task-specific heads. The second, Contrastive-MTL, provides implicit syntactic guidance through a contrastive auxiliary objective and a syntax-biased attention pooling mechanism, without requiring explicit label prediction. Both rely on syntactic annotations during training and eliminate need for hand-crafted compositional rules or external parsing at inference. We evaluate eleven datasets spanning seven languages---the MARC corpus (English, Spanish, French, German) and seven datasets from SemEval-2022 Task 10 (English, Spanish, Norwegian, Basque, Catalan)---using four established SEL encodings. With the relative encoding, Contrastive-MTL outperforms a syntax-naive baseline on 10 of 11 datasets and surpasses the external rule-based pipeline (SELSP) that parses at inference on all six datasets where the latter applies, while being 1.5--9$\times$ faster at evaluation. Standard-MTL is more dataset- and encoding-dependent. These results show implicit syntactic supervision during training can match or exceed explicit parsing at inference without computational overhead.

title_en: HaNDF: Object-Conditioned Geometric Neural Hand Distance Fields
abstract_en: We propose, HaNDF, object-conditional neural distance fields as data-driven priors for modeling the plausible hand-object configurations, in the product manifold of hand articulations. While recent unconditional generative priors showed success in modeling human pose, hands are versatile articulated bodies often found in interaction with other objects. This makes it crucial to develop a generative prior which can model the plausible hand poses conditioned on the object under interaction. To this end, our HaNDF proposes a geometry-aware, object-conditioned neural distance field, representing the plausible articulations in the zero-level set of a conditional field. We leverage tools from Riemannian geometry to (i) represent plausible hands in the zero level-set of an object-induced neural field, and (ii) project a given pose onto this field. Using HaNDF, we can also optimize for a plausible condition, determining the object under interaction. Our extensive evaluations demonstrate that our HaNDF provides a flexible and powerful prior for hand-object interaction, suitable for applications such as pose refinement, reconstruction under occlusion, and physically plausible manipulation synthesis.

title_en: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
abstract_en: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. Experiments see that law only through finite, partial and noisy interventions. We ask when such a quantity is identifiable from an experiment's access, continuous in the mechanism and certifiable from finite data, and answer exactly for a deliberately demanding case - the integrated information $\varphi$ of integrated information theory - in stochastic networks of four and five units with known ground truth. Behavior can be silent: a recurrent and a feed-forward network with identical input-output laws at their response delay carry 0.28 and 0 bits, yet internal recordings separate them within 4-53 trials. Partial access can be just as blind: in our examples, units left out of a one-step recording impose precision floors of 0.30-1.02 bits that no sample size lowers, and in all-but-self parity networks, recordings of any length see several hidden units only through the product of their fidelities - a symmetry that one intervention broke in exact checks. The measure has sharp edges: because $\varphi$ selects a partition, and the cause and effect it specifies, by one criterion and reports another, infinitesimal changes of mechanism that cross an edge change it by 25-100% at 99% of the edges we found in random networks, and about 1% of surrogate models that fit interventional data almost perfectly misreport it by more than 20%. One-sided claims survive: the same data certify a lower bound on both sides of an edge, and we prove $\varphi>1.004$ bits throughout a 64-dimensional region of mechanisms and certify it from about $10^7$ controlled transitions with false-certificate probability at most $α$. Measurability is thus a design question with computable answers.

title_en: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care
abstract_en: Designing healthcare strategies requires anticipating their clinical and operational consequences before implementation, a task that often relies on health system simulation. Such a simulation necessitates modeling how patient states evolve and generate care demands. However, conventional approaches typically tailor compact state transitions to a single policy question and omit history-dependent dynamics, thus requiring the redefinition of states and transitions when there is a new question that entails different clinical information. We propose to learn a patient world model from longitudinal EHRs using a neural network to provide a shared clinical representation of patient trajectories that can serve simulation questions across scenarios. Taking ICU operations as an example, we train the model on MIMIC-IV, freeze it, and couple its time-queryable predictions to shared ICU calendars, resources, and queues via scenario-specific mappings, so that one model renders admission demand, care tasks, and discharge proposals across simulations evaluating ICU bed capacity, care dispatch, and post-ICU transfer capacity. Experiments show that our model matches Markov and semi-Markov comparators in aggregate occupancy and directional responses to capacity and dispatch policies. It also reproduces policy gains from replayed observed trajectories. For patients entering the same support state from different prior trajectories, the learned representation captures a 24-h recovery difference (-6.4 predicted versus -6.7 observed percentage points), a contrast missed by compact state models, which propagates into distinct simulated care demand, queue burden, and bed use. These results indicate that a learned world model of patient dynamics has the potential to replace question-specific state models, allowing new care policies to be evaluated by reconfiguring the scenario without model rebuilding.

title_en: A Theoretical Analysis of a Bilevel Optimization Formulation for Combined Local-Global Optical Flow Models
abstract_en: This paper analyzes a bilevel formulation for learning the regularization parameter of combined local-global (CLG) optical flow models. The lower-level problem computes the flow from a Lucas--Kanade data term and a quadratic or total variation (TV) regularizer, and the upper-level problem selects the parameter that minimizes the squared distance to a ground-truth flow. The setting is finite-dimensional, and a full-rank assumption makes the lower-level solution unique. For the quadratic model we derive sufficient conditions for the existence of an optimal parameter, for every optimal parameter to be positive, and for strict local optimality. For TV regularization an optimal parameter always exists, because the lower-level solution vanishes for large parameters, and we give a sufficient condition for positivity that accounts for the coupling of the two flow components through the local structure tensors. Synthetic examples illustrate the conditions, including cases in which they fail.

title_en: Spectral Regimes of Truncated sinc-Power and Pulse-Train Kernels: Edge Exponents, Per-Edge Plunges, and the Landau-Widom Limit
abstract_en: A signal band-limited to one rectangular band and observed through a finite window is the classical concentration problem of Slepian, Landau, Pollak, and Widom. The eigenvalues of the operator cluster near one and near zero, separated by a transition called the plunge. The plunge width grows like the logarithm of the window length, with a universal coefficient of one over pi squared set by the band-edge jump. This paper follows the clusters and the plunge as the band is deformed. An elementwise power of the kernel smooths the band edge, and the plunge gives way to a power-law edge with exponent one less than the power. Disjoint copies of the band widen the plunge in proportion to the number of band edges, as the multiple-interval theorem of Landau and Widom implies, so the coefficient is a per-edge constant. Shrinking each band to a line gives the classical finite-rank operator. Overlapping bands give a multilevel staircase, and a self-similar band gives a cluster hierarchy governed by the Cantor dimension. At the smooth edge, rescaled eigenvalues do not collapse onto one curve. The edge descriptor passes from a constant to an exponent to an integer to a fractal dimension. For the single band, classical results place all eigenfilter zeros on the unit circle, with more of them inside the band as the order rises, so the dominant eigenvectors act as lowpass filters.

title_en: Core-Lock Scheduling for 5G NR LDPC Decoders
abstract_en: Accelerating iterative LDPC decoding while preserving error-correction reliability is a critical challenge in latency-constrained 5G New Radio (NR) and non-terrestrial networks. title_en: Electromagnetically Consistent Monostatic ISAC Beamforming: Mutual Coupling, Active Mismatch and Tx-Rx Leakage in Compact Dipole Arrays
abstract_en: Beamforming for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is usually designed on ideal array manifolds with a norm constraint on the transmit signal. title_en: Accelerating Safe Reinforcement Learning with Massive Parallelism
abstract_en: We investigate the problem of scaling safe reinforcement learning (safe RL) to massively parallel training regimes, where a large number of environments are exe- cuted with short rollout horizons. Using an MJX-based implementation of Safety Gym, our experiments show that the proposed method achieves performance comparable to non-massively parallel implementations while substantially reducing wall-clock training time.

title_en: Value-oriented policy distillation for interpretable wind farm power control
abstract_en: Wind farm power control can help the system maintain balance and avoid blackouts. In Europe, this can be achieved through implicit balancing, where a wind farm adjusts its power setpoint in anticipation of the imbalance price using information published by the Transmission System Operator. Thereby, the wind farm helps restore system balance while also reducing its own imbalance costs resulting from forecast errors. However, implicit balancing is a challenging problem since the settlement price is unknown in advance and can be impacted by the pursued control strategy. Reinforcement learning methods could help to solve this problem, but lack the interpretability needed to be deployed on real wind farms. Therefore, we propose a policy distillation framework using explainable boosting machines (EBMs), a variant of generalized additive models, to obtain a transparent control policy. To increase the value captured by the EBM model, we introduce a value-oriented perspective to policy distillation inspired by research in the field of energy forecasting. Furthermore, we suggest to include expert knowledge during model design, such that the control strategy is also justifiable to stakeholders. Using real data of the Belgian grid and an offshore wind farm, we find that our value-oriented and expert-based controller can reduce imbalance costs by 82%, while outperforming a price threshold controller as well as a policy distillation baseline using decision trees.

title_en: Spectral Convergence of Sparse Bipartite Graphs via the Line-Graphon
abstract_en: Pure point spectral convergence is generally unavailable for sparse graph sequences, where Laplacian eigenvalues may remain unstable under graph growth. title_en: Who Can Evaluate AI Independently? A Framework for Analysing Evaluation Infrastructure
abstract_en: AI evaluation is increasingly central to AI safety and governance, yet taking part in an evaluation does not by itself confer authority over its design, its execution or the resources it depends on. This paper examines how infrastructure arrangements distribute that authority, and so shape who can evaluate AI systems independently. Drawing on Science and Technology Studies, political economy and applied evaluation standards, we introduce PAAI (Power, Access, Adequacy, Independence), a framework for examining who controls evaluation infrastructure, the terms on which it is available, whether it is adequate to the evaluation's purpose and what autonomy it supports. We apply PAAI to twelve African AI evaluation projects (2022-2025) and to the documented roles of all ten member institutes in the three published joint testing exercises of the international network of AI Safety Institutes. We identify three recurring configurations: extractive collaboration, dependent innovation and constrained independence. African actors often contribute data, language expertise and task design while external institutions retain authority over infrastructure and evaluation frameworks; design authority without infrastructure authority never yielded more than partial independence. The joint testing exercises show a similar division among mostly high-income members: the institutes that led each exercise also ran the models, while Kenya, the network's only African member, moved from annotation to task design with no documented model execution. Participation in evaluation does not by itself produce evaluative authority. For evaluation to serve as a credible governance mechanism, access must come with control over priorities, methods, publication and continuity.

title_en: MUSS: A Multi-scale and Sequence-based Model for Single-cell Gene Regulation
abstract_en: Modeling gene regulation in single cells requires jointly representing DNA sequence, chromatin accessibility, and gene expression across regulatory scales. title_en: When Imperfect Automated Fact-Checking Backfires: Social Learning in the Presence of Misinformation
abstract_en: Automated fact-checking tools, cheap and fast but imperfect, are increasingly available on social platforms. title_en: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation
abstract_en: On-policy distillation (OPD) is emerging as an important paradigm for language-model post-training, combining dense teacher supervision with training on student-generated trajectories. This creates a feedback loop where each update changes the student and thereby the training distribution that generates subsequent updates. While OPD alone may degrade generation, it can yield substantial accuracy gains after sufficient offline preparation. title_en: Technohybridism: Recursive Semantic Normalization in AI-Mediated Societies
abstract_en: Language-generating AI systems are no longer only objects of linguistic interaction: their outputs increasingly re-enter the communicative and institutional practices from which their training material was drawn. Drawing on social theory, social epistemology, and the philosophy of language, this article develops a sociotechnical account of that re-entry. We introduce recursive semantic normalization: the process through which machine-generated formulations, once recurrently taken up, evaluated, reused, and institutionally retained, participate in the reproduction and transformation of semantic regularities. Under the heading of technohybridism, we argue that the relevant unit of analysis is the hybrid semantic system, a recursively coupled configuration of human practices, computational generation, and institutional uptake. First, we distinguish the concept from neighbouring accounts, including model collapse, looping effects, machine habitus, machine culture, and the epistemology of AI testimony. Second, we develop an analytical model that separates generation, selection, uptake, and persistence and distinguishes machine-attributable change from change that would have occurred anyway. Third, we analyse uptake as routinized, institutionally diffused, and socially stratified practice and state conditions under which machine-derived regularities become norms. Fourth, we identify social-epistemic consequences: the laundering of provenance that weakens epistemic vigilance, the erosion of the cognitive diversity on which collective inquiry depends, and the narrowing of shared hermeneutical resources. An evidential ladder for empirical research follows. The account attributes no normative authority to machine outputs; what changes is the field within which human and institutional uptake operates.

title_en: Geometry-Aware Channel Aging in MIMO Systems: When Is Kronecker Separability Enough?
abstract_en: This letter investigates when Kronecker-separable spatial correlation approximates the covariance of multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) channels. We propose a geometry-aware channel model in which the same propagation environment determines both the Weischelberger spatial coupling matrix and the temporal correlation coefficient. The propagation environment follows a 3GPP-inspired clustered channel model. We consider a MIMO system affected by symbol-level channel aging caused by the user equipment's mobility. We schedule both uplink and downlink pilots, thereby deriving the respective spectral efficiencies (SEs) in the presence of imperfect channel state information. Numerical results show that channel aging's magnitude is strongly geometry-dependent, with diffuse propagation inducing greater temporal decorrelation and SE degradation than concentrated scattering. The results also identify regimes where Kronecker separability can be applied and regimes where geometry-aware Weischelberger coupling is needed.

title_en: Phase-Matched Design of Pinching-Antenna Elements on a 60-GHz Dielectric Rod Waveguide
abstract_en: The radiation of pinching antennas, dielectric elements placed on a dielectric waveguide, depends on the element shape. We explain it with a phase-matching, or prism-coupler, picture: the guided rod mode couples into the denser antenna plate at an angle set by the plate-mode effective index, about 31 degrees at 60 GHz, and radiates through the face it reaches first. This yields a simple sizing rule linking element height to contact length. The rectangle peaks sharply at the rule, reaching 15.9 dBi. The right triangle keeps its gain within 0.7 dB and its side lobes at least 10 dB down over a two-to-one height range. At the rule, both outperform the isosceles element by 1.2 to 2.1 dB, and all remain matched.

title_en: Spatial Reuse in Multi-Cell Pinching-Antenna Systems
abstract_en: In this paper, spatial reuse in a multi-cell pinching-antenna system (PASS) is investigated, where each cell employs a dielectric waveguide with one activated pinching antenna (PA) to serve a single user. Spatial reuse refers to the simultaneous use of the same time-frequency resource block (RB) by multiple spatially separated cells. Due to inter-cell interference (ICI), simultaneous transmission by all cells on the same RB may be infeasible, and multiple RBs may be required to serve all users. The spatial-reuse capability is thus characterized by the minimum number of RBs required to satisfy all users' signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) targets under per-cell power budgets. Flexible PA placement can enhance the desired-link gain of each user and reduce the required transmit power of its serving cell, which in turn mitigates ICI and allows more cells to share the same RB. To exploit these benefits, a joint optimization problem of RB allocation, PA placement, and power control is formulated. For the two-cell case, the globally optimal PA placement is determined by minimizing the peak transmit power required by the two cells. A one-dimensional special case is further analyzed to derive analytical expressions for the average RB requirement and its scaling laws with respect to cell length under different PA-placement strategies. For the general multi-cell case, the optimal two-cell solution is exploited to construct a weighted compatibility graph, whose edge weights represent the minimum peak transmit powers required for feasible pairwise RB reuse. Based on this graph, a greedy RB allocation algorithm with minimum-weight pair initialization and element-wise PA-placement optimization is developed. Numerical results validate the analytical findings and demonstrate that PASS significantly reduces the required RBs compared with conventional fixed-antenna systems.

title_en: From Choirs to Solos: Reducing Multi-Cell Cooperation via Pinching Antennas
abstract_en: This article investigates the potential of the pinching-antenna system (PASS) to reduce multi-cell cooperation requirements. The cooperation cost is minimized subject to user signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio requirements and individual transmit-power constraints. title_en: Network Effect Decomposition for Causal Effect Estimation under Network Interference
abstract_en: Estimating causal effects from observational network data requires accounting for both individual treatment and neighborhood exposure. Existing outcome models commonly incorporate these intervention variables into a joint predictor and estimate causal effects through prediction contrasts, leaving the corresponding response components implicit. title_en: FARR: Forecast-Aware Residual Refinement with Matched Endpoint Evidence for Long-Horizon Time-Series Forecasting
abstract_en: Large language models use auxiliary conditioning to incorporate additional information into time-series forecasts. However, auxiliary conditioning does not consistently improve accuracy and can increase forecasting error when its influence is poorly matched to the observed temporal context. Horizon-wise gating then controls the contribution of the predicted residual to the final output. Experiments on four long-horizon forecasting benchmarks show that FARR achieves the best dataset-average MSE and MAE among the compared methods. title_en: Randomized Parallel Complexity of Weakly Convex Optimization
abstract_en: We study the minimum number of query rounds needed to find approximate stationary points of nonsmooth weakly convex functions, measured by the gradient of the Moreau envelope. Each round permits multiple simultaneous queries. title_en: Comparing Classification and Feature Learning by Analyzing Their Loss Functions in Normalized Spaces with Different Scale Factors
abstract_en: Classification and feature learning are two closely interrelated fundamental tasks. Feature learning in supervised settings is typically achieved by training classification models, under the common assumption that higher classification accuracy implies better feature quality. In this paper, we first point out that classification accuracy reflects the sample-wise local properties of a model on a dataset, whereas feature learning aims to learn features with good dataset-level global properties, such as intra-class compactness and inter-class separability. From the first principle of feature learning, we redesign the binary cross-entropy (BCE) loss, a counterpart of the cross-entropy (CE) loss used in classification. Then, in normalized feature space, we analyze the minima of the BCE and CE losses and show that both can lead to neural collapse, where sample features from different classes become maximally compact and maximally separated. More importantly, by investigating the convergence behaviors of the two losses as the scale factor $γ$ varies in the normalized space, we reveal how classification accuracy and feature quality change differently across spaces of different sizes. Under a fixed training strategy, a very large $γ$ achieves perfect classification accuracy but slows convergence toward the ideal feature geometry, whereas a very small $γ$ makes classification highly sensitive to small perturbations. A moderate $γ$ is therefore necessary for simultaneously achieving reliable classification and well-structured features. Extensive experiments validate these findings and demonstrate that BCE loss exhibits advantages in long-tail and open-set recognitions, as it better aligns with the global requirements of feature learning.

title_en: Selective Event Evidence and Persistent Temporal Priors for Event-Based Point Tracking
abstract_en: Event cameras enable tracking under fast motion and challenging illumination. However, stable long-term point tracking remains challenging: event activity is sparse and varies with scene content and motion, complicating correspondence, while trajectory estimates can drift over long sequences. Together, these challenges motivate a tracker that selectively uses informative event evidence and retains trajectory constraints across temporal windows. We propose Selective Event Evidence and Persistent Temporal Priors (SEPT), an event-only framework for tracking any point (TAP) over long sequences. SEPT introduces two complementary modules: Task-Adaptive Event Evidence Modulation (TEEM) and Persistent Trajectory Prior (PTP). Using only tracking supervision, TEEM learns a bounded reliability field that weights the event tensor across space, time, and channels before feature extraction. PTP carries geometric information across overlapping windows by marginalizing a fixed local quadratic trajectory model with a Schur complement. Its visibility-aware correction refines overlap coordinates, while a clipped terminal velocity initializes coordinates at newly exposed timestamps. SEPT builds on the ETAP architecture. SEPT is trained exclusively on synthetic EventKubric data and evaluated on five datasets across TAP and feature tracking. Results show that SEPT outperforms the retrained ETAP baseline in average Jaccard for TAP and in feature age and expected feature age for feature tracking; it also surpasses several methods combining event and frame inputs on EC and EDS. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/sssxxxkkkk/SEPT.
